summary: Oriented on the captured hashicorp/raft snapshot and traced one decision-support relationship: which configuration a restarted node uses for candidate admission and election quorum. Source reading showed NewRaft's post-restore configuration scan starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 while the new RestoreCommittedLogs replay raises lastApplied to the log store's persisted commit index first, so a committed configuration entry newer than the last snapshot is never processed. Filed 14 sources, one active question on that scan/replay interaction (plus a second registered question on replay backpressure in the constructor), four behavior/fact entries, and one experiment whose harness builds the same restart-shaped stores twice (feature off vs on, plus a live-node sample) with separate mode admissions and an assertion that the node's latest configuration equals the committed configuration entry in its own log. Local construction feedback showed the predicted split (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} index 1, quorum 2, live node reporting {A,B,C}), and the update validates; the retained receipt must confirm it before the question-level account moves off conditional. Incomplete: the retained execution, its comparison interpretation, an executed multi-node witness for the minority-quorum consequence, and the second registered question's discriminator.
